answers: lens-correctness-design finding 1: nothing to do — Finding 22 of the design already addresses this. The proposed guard `${_ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE:-false} == true` in `_cycle_dispatch` was step 7a, which the design explicitly removes as WRONG. cycle-orchestrator.sh:2343 consumes the flag (`_ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE=false`) before the iteration loop starts, so the flag is always false when `_cycle_dispatch` is called. The correct and final form is the existing `if [[ "$_cd_iter" -gt 0 ]]; then` guard, which emits `stage.start` for all cycle member dispatches at iter > 0 — covering stage k during resume (DSPK-1) and all iters in fresh runs. The Gap 7 entry in the design is explicitly labelled "DESIGN CORRECTION" and removes step 7a.

lens-red-team-design finding 1: nothing to do — the design already states this explicitly in Finding 22 and in the "Key structural facts" in the notes. `_ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE` is intentionally single-use: its sole purpose is `_start_iter` selection in the cycle orchestrator; it is consumed (set false) immediately after that selection; it is NOT a "this dispatch is part of a resume" broadcast. The CMBR-1 fix (Gap 9) intentionally does NOT use this flag — it uses a local `resume_first_iter` argument passed from the orchestrator to `_cycle_dispatch`, precisely because the flag has already been consumed by that point. The design captures this in both the Decision section and in Finding 22's structural fact #1.
